label: 🚀 Quick start
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🚀 Quick start[/color][/font_size]

Welcome to [b]Dungeon Editor[/b]: a first-person dungeon-crawling game with real-time turn-based combat and a party of heroes to grow — and, if you wish, an online side (rankings, rewards, chat). The rest of this guide covers every element; here is what you need to get going.

[b]1. Choose how to play[/b] (home screen)
  • [b]Random Dungeon[/b] — the big central seal: a different dungeon every time. With an account, the [b]Challenges[/b] window opens first (rankings, ranked runs, rewards); you then launch the dungeon with the usual settings.
  • [b]The Original Dungeon[/b] — the official 3-level demo, ideal for learning.
  • [b]Create your own dungeon[/b] — the editor (Admin) to build an adventure from scratch. The “New here?” link opens the creation tutorial.
  • [b]Saves[/b] — resume one of your games.

[b]2. First steps in game[/b]
  • Move with the [b]arrow keys[/b] or [b]WASD[/b] (ZQSD in French), turn, and walk up to a monster: [b]Space[/b] attacks, keys [b]2 to 7[/b] cast the active hero's spells.
  • Click a [b]portrait[/b] to pick the active hero; the chest icon opens their inventory.
  • Open the [b]minimap[/b] full-screen with [b]M[/b]; save from the Save menu.
  • To leave a level you need the arch key (carried by the level's boss or its toughest monster).

[b]3. The top bar[/b] (always visible)

[b]4. Online play is optional[/b]
The whole game stays playable [b]without an account and offline[/b]. A free account adds [b]rankings[/b], verified [b]ranked runs[/b], [b]experience[/b] and [b]badges[/b] with their cosmetics, and the [b]chat[/b].

💡 Lost? Look for the topic in the list above: every window of the game has its page in this guide.

label: 🏠 The home screen
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🏠 The home screen[/color][/font_size]

In the centre, the [b]« Random dungeon » seal[/b] (the dice roll when you hover it) generates a different dungeon every time. Once signed in to an account, the seal is called [b]« Expedition »[/b] (« ranked or free »). On the right, three banners: [b]Create your own dungeon[/b] (a random base you can freely edit in the admin), [b]The Original Dungeon[/b] (the official 3-level demo) and [b]Save slots[/b] (your 10 slots).

Two discreet links complete the screen: « Load a dungeon from a code » and « Import a JSON file ». Under « Create your own dungeon », the « 🧭 New here? » link opens the creation tutorial.

At the bottom: the [b]version number[/b] (click it to open the version log) and the [b]build identifier[/b] (date and time the file was delivered — compare it if you doubt you have the latest version).

While exploring, a small badge under the level name shows the [b]dungeon type[/b]: Original, Random or Custom.

🌐 [b]Top bar and online play[/b]: the top bar (folded to the right when not hovered; tap ◂ on mobile) groups Home, Guide, Settings, [b]💬 Chat[/b], [b]👤 Account[/b], Admin and the language. The “Random Dungeon” seal first opens the [b]Challenges[/b] window (rankings, ranked runs, rewards) when the online service is available — see “Challenges and ranked runs”.

label: 🧭 Moving around
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🧭 Moving around and exploring[/color][/font_size]

The compact d-pad at the bottom-left of the game screen lets you [b]move forward[/b], [b]move back[/b] and [b]turn[/b] (left/right). You can also use the [b]arrow keys[/b] or [b]WASD[/b] — the pressed key briefly lights up on the pad.

The [b]minimap[/b] (top-right during play) shows already-explored areas. On a large dungeon, a small hint [b]'Wheel: zoom in / out'[/b] appears at the bottom of the map: the mouse wheel (or a double-click; double-tap on touch screens) zooms in and out.

Some [b]doors[/b] are locked: you need to find the matching key (often carried by a guardian monster) or another condition set by the adventure to open them.

A level's [b]exit arch[/b] (the one leading to the next level) is also sealed by an iron gate in a randomly generated dungeon. The key is always carried by the level's [b]boss[/b] if there is one (in addition to their usual loot), or by its toughest monster otherwise — never a random search through every room.

[b]Traps[/b] are sometimes hidden around a room — a plain, subtle dark mark, barely visible on the floor. Arriving on one opens a [b]lockpicking[/b] window (see “Traps and lockpicking”); a disarmed trap disappears for good, and a single-use trap no longer reactivates once triggered.

💡 Monsters also move on their own within a zone around them, even without you acting — scout the corridor before rushing in!

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Second wind (exploration regeneration)[/color][/font_size]

Out of combat your heroes recover while walking: every [b]N steps onto recent tiles[/b], each living hero regains [b]1% of max HP[/b] (at least 1), shown as a green "+1" on their card. N is 6 (easy), 8 (normal), 12 (hard) or 20 (nightmare). Regeneration stops at [b]60% of max HP[/b]: beyond that you need a potion, a healing spell or a fountain. Priests and druids (and their evolutions) regenerate 25% faster; Constitution adds +0.1% per point above 10.

It does not run while poisoned or burning, during the 2 steps after a combat, and retracing your last steps does not count. It can be turned off in the administration (General tab).

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Large dungeons[/color][/font_size]

Dungeons up to 60×60 tiles stay smooth: scenery and torches are only drawn where the camera looks, and distant 3D torches are hidden in the fog.

A big ⏸ symbol appears; a click anywhere, or [b]P[/b], [b]Esc[/b], [b]Space[/b] or [b]Enter[/b] resumes. In ranked games and challenges, the time spent paused is added to the game time sent to the leaderboard.

label: ⚔️ Combat
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]⚔️ Combat[/color][/font_size]

Each character has their own [b]⚔ Attack[/b] icon on their card, at the top-left of their portrait. A monster must be right in front of the party.

Combat follows an [b]initiative system in rounds[/b]: every character and every monster has a [b]Speed[/b] stat (see the dedicated topic) that fills its turn gauge. The faster a participant is, the earlier it acts — but [b]nobody acts again until every other living participant has acted once[/b]: that is a round. As soon as everyone has acted, a new round starts. Within a round the fastest acts first; at equal speed, heroes go before monsters. The order only changes if a speed changes (bonus or penalty) or a fighter dies.

A [b]visual queue[/b] always shows who acts next: vertical on the left side of the game screen (desktop), horizontal above the cards (mobile). Whoever's turn it is always sits at the end of the queue (bottom, on desktop), highlighted with a golden glow; as soon as they act, their portrait slides out and everyone else moves up one slot. The queue always shows a few turns ahead, never freezing.

Attacking costs a little [b]stamina[/b] (blue bar on each card), but the basic physical attack always remains possible, even with no stamina left — only spells and abilities can be blocked for lack of stamina. Stamina regenerates as you move or take hits.

[b]Monsters don't stay passive[/b]: they patrol on their own within a zone around their starting position, even without you acting, and chase you if they spot you. Once adjacent, a monster stops moving and simply waits its turn in the queue, just like your characters.

Some monsters appear in a [b]group[/b] (2 or 3 side by side in the corridor, each with its own HP bar). Every living member is a full participant: it acts [b]once per round[/b], at the monster's speed, like any hero. Its difficulty comes from its number of attacks per round, its higher total HP and the improved loot it drops.

On contact with a monster, a [b]dedicated combat window[/b] opens full-screen, over everything else (map, log, inventory): the dungeon fully pauses (no other monster moves or approaches) while it's open. The backdrop becomes a small sealed arena matching the level's theme. A [b]group[/b] of monsters is shown in full, side by side — click one (soft light-blue glow; red is reserved for rage) to set the target for the next attack. A small [b]potion pouch[/b] appears under the portraits so you can heal without opening the full inventory — [b]scrolls[/b] are there too: they instantly cast a spell once, for free and regardless of class, before being consumed.

The [b]🏃 Flee[/b] button, at the bottom-right of the combat screen, lets you abandon the current fight at any time. A confirmation is required: fleeing moves the party to a nearby spot out of sight of the fought monster (never triggering an immediate new fight), at the cost of [b]50% of the whole party's current stamina[/b].

A [b]turn timer[/b] (red bar under the Flee button) limits thinking time: when it reaches zero, the turn passes automatically to the next one. It applies to characters and monsters alike; its duration (3 to 10 seconds) is set in the admin's General tab, where it can also be disabled.

Click a [b]monster's name[/b] during a fight to open its info window: the game pauses and you see the stats, HP and active statuses of each member of the monster group. Close the window to resume.

On victory, a summary screen recaps monsters defeated, XP, gold, loot, and remaining party HP before returning to exploration. On defeat, a dedicated screen also appears, regardless of when in the fight it happens.

💡 Outside combat (no monster engaged), freely select any character by clicking their card. As soon as combat starts, selection becomes automatic again and strictly follows the queue — you can't click another character until it's their turn.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Basic attack[/color][/font_size]

Hover the ⚔ attack disc to see its [b]damage[/b], its [b]crit chance[/b], any life steal and its stamina cost.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Survival instinct[/color][/font_size]

When a direct monster hit (attack or ability) would drop a hero, combat freezes: a [b]red button[/b] appears on the left side of the view, with a shrinking ring and the remaining time counting down inside the disc. Press it (click, [b]Space[/b] or [b]Enter[/b]) [b]as late as possible[/b] before the ring ends: the later the press, the better the odds (last third = "perfect"). A dice roll then decides: [b]success[/b] = the hero survives with 1 HP; [b]perfect[/b] = keeps 15% of max HP and triggers a class effect (Warrior: returns half the blow; Archer and Rogue: dodge it entirely; Mage: shield of 20% max HP; Priest and Druid: heal 10%; Bard: +10 stamina to the whole party). The hero is then [b]Dazed[/b] for 2 turns.

Once per hero per combat; traps, poison or burn, and stunned, frozen or sleeping heroes never qualify. The window lasts 3.5 s (easy), 3 s (normal), 2.5 s (hard), 2 s (hardcore). In [b]⚙ Settings[/b]: mode On / Auto (reduced chance) / Off, and window ×1, ×1.5 or ×2. In ranked runs, settings and rules are identical for everyone.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Numbers and monster deaths[/color][/font_size]

Damage numbers stack: on the monster for what it takes, above the hero's card for what the hero takes (bigger, outside the frame). A slain monster falls at the end of the spell effect, not during it.

label: 💨 Speed
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]💨 The Speed stat[/color][/font_size]

[b]Speed[/b] is its own stat, separate from Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, or Intelligence. It [b]only[/b] determines turn order in the initiative queue (see the ⚔️ Combat topic): the higher it is, the earlier the participant acts in the round. It never increases the number of turns in a round, which stays at one per participant. It does not affect damage or HP.

On a hand-placed monster (Admin mode), Speed is an editable field. Left empty, it is 8 modified by the monster's Dexterity (+1 per 3 points above 9). For a character, the Admin sheet lets you override the class speed; each class speed is set in the Classes tab.

Conversely, the [b]🐌 Slow[/b] spell removes -4 Speed from an enemy for 3 turns.

💡 No dice roll enters this calculation: at equal stats, two participants always act in the same order. Open a character sheet (🎒 icon, then Statistics) to see its speed broken down: class, gear, effects.

label: 📊 Statistics
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]📊 Statistics[/color][/font_size]

Everything is shown as-is: the game hides no calculation. Every value derives from five attributes ([b]Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Speed[/b]), each equal to [b]Base + Gear + Talents + Statuses[/b].

[b]Where to see them[/b]

  • [b]Character sheet[/b] (🎒 icon on the card, then the [b]Statistics[/b] tab): the attribute table (Base, Gear, Talents, Statuses, Total, and what the total gives in combat), then the [b]Combat[/b] section: HP, stamina, attack, crit, dodge, guard, reductions, spell power, lifesteal.
  • [b]Inventory[/b] (key [b]I[/b]): the [b]Characteristics[/b] frame summarizes HP, stamina, attack, Str / Dex / Con / Int, speed, crit / dodge / guard and spell power; the [b]Details and spells[/b] button adds more.
  • [b]Character card[/b] (hover in the bottom bar): each attribute is followed by its base and modifiers, e.g. "Dex · 12 +2" (green if raised, red if lowered).
  • [b]Monster sheet[/b] (click its name in combat, or the Bestiary).

[b]The hover window.[/b] Hover a statistic (sheet, inventory or monster sheet): a window opens, organized in [b]cards[/b], one per statistic. Each card contains, from top to bottom:

  • the [b]header[/b]: icon, name and final value;
  • the [b]rule[/b], in one sentence;
  • the [b]calculation[/b] line by line: Base, Gear, Talents, Statuses, Total (bonuses in green, penalties in red);
  • the [b]worked formulas[/b] with your values ("Crit = 16 − 10 → 6 %") and, when there is one, the [b]cap[/b];
  • the [b]modifier sources[/b]: each equipped item (with its icon and slot), each talent and each active status (with remaining turns) and what it adds. If nothing modifies the value, it says so.

[b]Item effects, hero by hero.[/b] In the [b]Combat[/b] section of the sheet, the [b]six school resistances[/b] (Physical, Fire, Ice, Nature, Holy, Shadow) and the [b]seven perks of rare items[/b] (spell damage, execute, bleed, critical damage, thorns, gold, last stand) are always listed, even at 0. Hover one: the card shows the rule, the calculation (class bonus + equipment, or the total of the rarity perks) and [b]every equipped item that grants it[/b], with its value. A negative resistance is a weakness; it is limited to −50% … +90%. The [b]📊 Details and spells[/b] drawer of the inventory also holds a [b]Bonuses and effects[/b] section: everything that improves the hero, grouped (attributes, combat, school resistances, item perks, mythic set, talents, active statuses, class, Constitution and expedition modifiers), with [b]every source[/b] under each line (item and slot, talent, status, class) and its share. Anything with no effect is summed up as 'No effect for now'.

When a row groups several values (Str / Dex / Con / Int, for instance), the cards sit side by side and wrap on narrow screens; the window always stays fully visible.

[b]The rules, one by one[/b]

[table=3][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Statistic[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Effect[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Calculation[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]💪 Strength  [/cell][cell]Minimum damage  [/cell][cell]⌊Str ÷ 3⌋ + ⌊(level − 1) ÷ 2⌋  [/cell][cell]🎯 Dexterity  [/cell][cell]Maximum damage  [/cell][cell]minimum + 2 + ⌊Dex ÷ 4⌋  [/cell][cell]🎯 Dexterity  [/cell][cell]Critical chance  [/cell][cell]+1 % per point above 10 (cap 25 %), plus talents, rare-item perks and mythic set  [/cell][cell]🎯 Dexterity  [/cell][cell]Dodging a monster's physical attack  [/cell][cell]⌊(Dex − 10) × 0.8⌋ % (cap 20 %)  [/cell][cell]🛡️ Constitution  [/cell][cell]Hit points  [/cell][cell]10 + 3 × Con + 4 per level gained (gear and talents on top)  [/cell][cell]🛡️ Constitution  [/cell][cell]Guard: reduces all damage taken  [/cell][cell]+1 % per point above 10 (cap 25 %)  [/cell][cell]✨ Intelligence  [/cell][cell]Spell power  [/cell][cell]⌊Int ÷ 3⌋ − 1 (Int 10 = +2)  [/cell][cell]⚡ Speed  [/cell][cell]Turn order within the round  [/cell][cell]class + gear + statuses  [/cell][/table]

Dexterity, Constitution and Intelligence bonuses only start above 10: below that, a low attribute is not penalized further.

[b]Combat values[/b]

  • [b]Attack[/b]: minimum – maximum damage, base + gear + talents.
  • [b]Crit[/b]: chance to double damage (Dexterity + talents).
  • [b]Dodge[/b]: chance to avoid a monster's physical attack entirely.
  • [b]Guard[/b]: reduction of all damage taken, from Constitution.
  • [b]Physical / magic reduction[/b]: talent resistance + guard, [b]capped at 75 %[/b].
  • [b]Spell power[/b]: [b]damage and healing[/b] get Intelligence + gear and talent spell damage + ⌊(level − 1) × 0.75⌋; [b]shields[/b] and [b]stamina restores[/b] only get the Intelligence part.
  • [b]Lifesteal[/b]: share of damage dealt returned as HP (talents, spells).

[b]In other tooltips[/b]

  • [b]Item[/b] (hover in the bag or inventory): each bonus is compared with the worn item, then a line gives the [b]real consequence[/b] for that character, e.g. "→ max HP +6 · guard +2 %" or "→ crit +1 % · dodge +0 %".
  • [b]Spell[/b]: the spell's base, plus the caster's power (Intelligence, gear, level), gives the [b]real[/b] damage, healing or shield ("Base 8 – 12 + power +3 = 11 – 15"); the tooltip also says that the target's resistance reduces damage, and that only Intelligence counts for shields and stamina.

[b]Monsters[/b]: HP = 5 + 2.8 × Con; minimum damage = max(1, ⌊Str ÷ 2.5⌋); maximum damage = minimum + 1 + ⌊Dex ÷ 3.3⌋; speed = the sheet's value, otherwise 8 + round((Dex − 9) ÷ 3). Their resistances reduce damage taken accordingly; active statuses (weakened, vulnerable…) are listed in the hover window.

💡 No hidden dice roll in these calculations, apart from the damage, critical and dodge draws.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Item perks and resistances[/color][/font_size]

[b]Item perks[/b] (crit, dodge, life steal…) are counted in the combat values of the sheet and detailed in the tooltip (« Equipment rarity » line). The other perks — spell damage, execute, poison, critical damage, thorns, gold gained, last stand — get their own cell on the sheet when you wear them.

🛡️ [b]Resistances per school[/b]: each class has its bonuses and small weaknesses (Warrior: physical; Druid: nature, but weak to fire; Mage: shadow/arcane, but weak to physical…), plus those of the items. They appear on the sheet (one cell per school, « + » resists, « − » weakness) and reduce (or increase) the damage of the matching school.

label: ✨ Spells and abilities
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]✨ Spells and abilities[/color][/font_size]

If a character knows at least one spell or ability, the [b]✨[/b] icon appears on their card. Click it to open a popup listing all their spells: clicking one casts it immediately (or, for a targeted heal, prepares the ally selection — see below).

Each spell can deal [b]damage[/b], provide a [b]single-target heal[/b], or a [b]party-wide heal[/b]. Every class has at least one ability (even physical classes like the Warrior), not just Mages and Priests.

Two special spells act on [b]Speed[/b] (see the dedicated topic) instead of HP: [b]💨 Haste[/b] (Priest, level 6) speeds up an ally, and [b]🐌 Slow[/b] (Mage, level 6) slows an enemy while dealing a bit of damage.

For a [b]targeted heal[/b]: after picking the spell in the popup, a golden banner appears above the cards — click directly on the ally's card to heal them (a pulsing golden outline shows which cards are selectable). A Cancel button lets you back out without casting.

Each spell has its own [b]cooldown[/b] (shown in the popup if not yet ready) and its own [b]stamina cost[/b] (the more powerful the spell, the higher the cost) — nothing stops you from opening the popup any time, but a spell still on cooldown or without enough stamina will refuse to cast.

[b]Shortcuts[/b]: keys [b]2[/b] to [b]7[/b] cast the active character's spells, in combat [b]and in exploration[/b] (heals, protections…). Hover a spell to see its base, the caster's power and the real total (see 📊 Statistics).

[b]Scrolls[/b] found in-game let you teach a new spell to a compatible character, from the bag.

label: 🧪 Status effects
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🧪 Status effects[/color][/font_size]

Some spells and abilities (from players [b]and[/b] monsters) can inflict an effect in addition to their damage:

  • 🧪 [b]Poison[/b] and 🔥 [b]Burn[/b]: extra damage each turn — [b]and keep going even outside combat[/b], with every step taken, not just during a fight.
  • 😵 [b]Stun[/b] and ❄️ [b]Freeze[/b]: the victim skips their next action turn.
  • 💨 [b]Haste[/b] and 🐌 [b]Slow[/b]: temporarily raises or lowers Speed, and so how often turns come around.
  • 📉 [b]Weakened[/b] and 😣 [b]Vulnerable[/b] (Bard spells): the monster deals less damage (−35% on its next hit for Weakened); Vulnerable also lowers its resistances for several turns.
  • 🎶 [b]Vigor[/b]: new negative statuses received last half as long.
  • 🔥 [b]Flaming Blade[/b]: flat bonus damage on every weapon hit.

[b]Only one active status at a time[/b]: a new status always replaces a different status already in progress — they never stack (e.g. burn and freeze can never both be active on the same character).

A [b]burning[/b] or [b]poisoned[/b] character shows a clearly visible colored label on their card (red for burn, green for poison), without preventing healing. A [b]frozen[/b] character shows a large "Frozen" label (like the death indicator): no potion can be used on them and they can't be targeted by a healing spell until the effect passes — the rest of the party can still keep exploring normally.

💡 If the whole party ends up stunned/frozen at once [b]during combat[/b], the turn passes automatically so you never get stuck.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Effects stay visible for their whole duration[/color][/font_size]

As long as a status lasts, its effect stays on screen: on a [b]monster[/b] (💤 rising « Z »s for [b]Sleep[/b], green bubbles for poison, real flames licking the body for burn, frost for freeze, stars for stun, arrows for weaken…) as well as on a [b]hero's card[/b]. The effect goes away when the status ends: a monster put to sleep for 3 turns keeps its « Z »s for 3 turns.

💤 [b]Sleep[/b]: the minstrel's [b]lullaby[/b] puts an ordinary monster to sleep (it skips its turns, for half of the spell's duration); a [b]boss[/b] is only slowed.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Statuses inflicted by monsters[/color][/font_size]

Depending on its [b]family[/b], a monster may inflict a status on heroes with its hits, with a given chance on each hit that lands: 🧪 poison (spider, naga, zombie, werewolf), 📉 weaken (mummy, cultist), 🐌 slow (skeleton archer, mud golem, slime), 🖤 life drain (ghost), 😵 stun (gargoyle, stone golem, troll, ogre, minotaur, mimic), 🔥 burn (fire elemental, imp, drake, hellcat), ❄️ freeze (ice elemental), 😣 vulnerable (harpy), 💤 sleep or freeze (beholder). Rats, goblins, wolves, orcs, gnolls, skeletons and lizardmen have none.

It is [b]random[/b]: from one level to another, the same monster sometimes has its effect and sometimes not. [b]Bosses[/b] always have one, more frequent and longer. The monster's sheet (click its name) shows « Inflicts: … ».

On a hero, 📉 [b]Weakened[/b] and 😣 [b]Vulnerable[/b] reduce their damage and their protection.

[b]Monster groups.[/b] In a group, each monster has its own statuses. A single-target spell (a fireball, for example) applies burn, poison, freeze or sleep only to the targeted monster; an area spell, or the lullaby, applies them to every monster in the group (one chance roll per monster). Turn countdown, damage over time and incapacitation are played out on each one when it acts: a monster can die of burning while the others still stand. The visual effect (flames, frost…) only appears on affected monsters, and their sheet lists the statuses line by line.

label: 🎒 Items and equipment
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🎒 Items and equipment[/color][/font_size]

The [b]party's shared bag[/b] (12 items max per tab, side panel during play) is shared by everyone, but it is now only a [b]preview[/b]: it lists item names (hover one for its detailed tooltip) with no buttons. Equipping, using and discarding are done in a character's inventory.

Each character card carries a [b]chest[/b] icon (next to the level): it opens their [b]inventory[/b], a drawer sliding in from the right over the game (the [b]I[/b] key opens the selected hero's). It shows the character surrounded by their slots, their stats, and the bag in three tabs (🗡️ weapons, armor and jewelry · 🧪 potions · 🗝️ keys and scrolls). Click an item: the slots it can be equipped in light up, and the card shows a [b]comparison[/b] with the item currently worn (+ in green, − in red). Click the glowing slot (or “Equip”, or the item again) to equip it; the previous item goes back to the bag. An item the class can't use is greyed out with the reason. The round buttons at the top of the drawer switch between characters without closing it, and the [b]📊 Details and spells[/b] button unrolls a drawer below the inventory with the character's stats, spells and abilities (on mobile, a window opens over the top). The game is paused while the drawer is open.

🔒 The inventory (equipment, bag potions) is [b]unavailable during combat[/b]. The 🎒 quick bar under the portraits then lets you drink a potion or read a scroll on the active hero.

6 equipment slots per character: [b]Weapon, Helmet, Armor, Gloves, Boots, Jewelry[/b]. There are no class restrictions: it's up to the player to decide who wears what. An item can also carry a [b]💨 Speed[/b] bonus (see the dedicated topic) — mostly boots and jewelry, more rarely a heavy weapon or heavy armor.

[b]Healing potions[/b] restore HP, [b]stamina potions[/b] (same design, in blue) restore stamina; [b]scrolls[/b] teach a spell. In the bag, potions of the [b]exact same value[/b] automatically group into a single line with a count (e.g. "Healing potion (+8 HP) ×5") — two potions with the same name but a different value (found at different depths) always stay on separate lines.

Rare [b]legendary items[/b] ✨ (unique name, shimmering gold) can appear as boss loot in randomly generated dungeons. Besides higher stats, they always carry a special bonus: 🩸 [b]Lifesteal[/b] (recovers part of the damage dealt as HP), 💥 [b]Critical[/b] (chance to double damage), or 🌵 [b]Thorns[/b] (reflects part of the damage taken back to the attacker).

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Item resistances[/color][/font_size]

[b]Epic[/b], [b]legendary[/b] (1 resistance) and [b]mythic[/b] (2) armor and jewelry may grant a [b]resistance to a school[/b] (fire, ice, nature, holy, shadow/arcane, physical), shown under the item's name. It adds to that of the wearer's class.

label: ⭐ Levels and evolution
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]⭐ Levels and evolution[/color][/font_size]

Each hero is shown by their [b]portrait[/b] on their card (portrait, name, class, level). Among 48 portraits (8 per base class), the random dungeon draws a different one for each party member; the Original Dungeon has fixed portraits; in a hand-made dungeon you pick each hero's in the admin. The portrait is kept on evolution.

XP earned from killing a monster is [b]split according to each character's actual contribution[/b] to that fight — not divided equally among everyone.

Leveling up increases [b]HP[/b] and [b]attack power[/b] (physical and spells). Some spells are learned automatically at specific levels. Progression is capped at [b]level 30[/b].

At [b]level 5[/b], a character can [b]evolve[/b] into one of two specialized paths tied to their starting class (e.g. Warrior → Berserker or Paladin). The choice is final. The window opens [b]as soon as combat ends[/b] (no need to act first) and shows each class with its [b]icon[/b] and description; once chosen, the character card's class, icon and color are updated.

The [b]Bard[/b] evolves into a [b]Skald[/b] (melee and offensive support) or a [b]Minstrel[/b] (magic support and control): dedicated spells, statuses and talents (see « Status effects »).

At [b]levels 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25[/b], a character is also offered a [b]talent[/b] to choose between two class-specific options (stat bonuses, HP, stamina, damage, critical chance, lifesteal, or resistance) — a dedicated window opens as soon as the level is reached, and a talent chosen before a class evolution stays acquired afterward. Talents already chosen are visible in each character's stats tooltip.

Once [b]every level of the dungeon is completed[/b], a victory screen appears — its content differs depending on the dungeon type:

[b]Randomly generated dungeon[/b] (via "🎲 Generate a random dungeon"):

  • 🛒 [b]Visit the shop[/b] — spend the gold gathered before moving on (see the dedicated topic).
  • ⚔️ [b]Continue into a harder dungeon[/b] — a new dungeon is generated, fully keeping the party: levels, evolved classes, spells, equipment and bag. The [b]dungeon's size[/b] (number of levels, width, height) stays exactly the same as what was chosen at the very start — only [b]difficulty[/b] rises, expedition after expedition, never going back down:

The difficulty tier chosen for the very first dungeon (Easy/Normal/Hard/Hardcore) sets a [b]starting multiplier[/b] applied to these same stats:

[table=2][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Tier[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Starting multiplier[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]Easy  [/cell][cell]×0.6  [/cell][cell]Normal  [/cell][cell]×1  [/cell][cell]Hard  [/cell][cell]×1.7  [/cell][cell]Hardcore  [/cell][cell]×3.0  [/cell][/table]

[b]Monster count[/b] per level follows a deliberately gentler multiplier — an identical multiplier to the stats one would make the very first corridor of a Hardcore dungeon impassable:

[table=2][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Tier[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Monster count multiplier[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]Easy  [/cell][cell]×0.7  [/cell][cell]Normal  [/cell][cell]×1  [/cell][cell]Hard  [/cell][cell]×1.35  [/cell][cell]Hardcore  [/cell][cell]×1.8  [/cell][/table]

Both multipliers then grow the same way with each expedition (+15% cumulative, see below).

[table=2][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]What grows with each expedition[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Detail[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]Monster Strength / Dex / Constitution  [/cell][cell]+15% cumulative per expedition, uncapped  [/cell][cell]XP and gold rewards  [/cell][cell]+15% cumulative per expedition  [/cell][cell]Quality of bonuses on found items  [/cell][cell]+15% cumulative per expedition  [/cell][cell]Legendary item chance  [/cell][cell]Gradual rather than a flat fixed tier  [/cell][/table]

In practice, a party that runs 5 expeditions in a row faces noticeably tougher monsters than on the first, even though the starting difficulty tier (Easy/Normal/Hard/Hardcore) never changes — that tier only sets the [b]starting point[/b] of this progression, not a ceiling. This option disappears once the whole party reaches level 30.

  • 🔄 [b]Start over[/b] — begins a brand new game.
  • 🏠 [b]Back to home[/b] — simply leaves the current game.

[b]Original Dungeon or hand-crafted dungeon[/b] (via admin): only "🔄 Start over" and "🏠 Back to home" are offered — the shop and continuing into a harder dungeon only make sense for a randomly generated dungeon.

In a randomly generated dungeon, the monsters encountered follow a [b]consistent progression[/b] based on depth: early levels favor more common foes (goblins, wolves, orcs...), the middle of the dungeon brings in more unusual threats (ghosts, imps, harpies, minotaurs...), and the final levels reserve the most fearsome creatures (elementals, beholders, stone golems...). This progression is based on the level's [i]relative[/i] depth in the dungeon, not its absolute number — so each "Continue into a harder dungeon" restarts its own power curve from the beginning, rather than dropping fearsome monsters onto the first level of an advanced expedition. Every so often, a monster from another tier can still appear, growing rarer as the progression gap widens — nothing is ever fixed at 100%.

💡 On the defeat screen (whole party fallen), a "📂 Load last save" button also appears if a save exists, to resume where you left off instead of starting over.

💡 The 📖 icon next to the event log (during play) opens the complete history of the whole adventure — everything is kept, expedition after expedition, up to level 30 if you go that far.

📊 The statistics icon (top-right of the game screen, next to sound) opens a full dashboard at any time, in three tabs: "Overview" (party, combat, wealth, progress), "Characters" (who's most active or most neglected, comparison charts, detailed sheet for each), and "📖 Bestiary" (details of every monster species defeated so far). These same statistics also display automatically on the victory screen.

🔇 No sound on mobile despite the 🔊 icon being on? Check the device's [b]silent/mute mode[/b] (physical switch on the side of an iPhone, or the volume shortcut on Android) as well as its [b]physical volume[/b] — these settings can mute the game independently of what's set inside the app.

⏸️ The game automatically pauses (monsters stop acting) during the class evolution, talent choice, trap-lockpicking, and fountain-use popups, as well as while viewing the inventory or stats — giving you time to think or browse calmly.

label: 🧮 Formulas & rates
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🧮 Formulas & rates — full reference[/color][/font_size]

All exact engine values, especially for the random dungeon generator. [code]i[/code] is the level index (0 = first level), [code]run[/code] the expedition number (1 for the very first).

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Character stats[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Max HP[/b] = 10 + Constitution×3 + (Level−1)×4
  • [b]Base min damage[/b] = ⌊Strength / 3⌋ + ⌊(Level−1)/2⌋
  • [b]Base max damage[/b] = min damage + 2 + ⌊Dexterity / 4⌋
  • [b]Max stamina[/b] = class base (usually 100) + talent bonuses
  • [b]Dexterity crit[/b] = 1 % per Dex point above 10 (max 25 %); [b]dodge[/b] = ⌊0.8 × (Dex − 10)⌋ % (max 20 %) against monsters' physical attacks
  • [b]Constitution guard[/b] = 1 % per Con point above 10 (max 25 %): reduces all damage taken
  • [b]Spell power[/b] = ⌊Int / 3⌋ − 1 (min 0; Int 10 = +2): added to damage, healing, shields and stamina restored. Damage and healing also get the gear/talent bonus and ⌊(Level−1) × 0.75⌋
  • [b]Effective speed[/b] = class base speed (or the speed set in Admin for the character) + gear bonus + temporary status bonus (Haste/Slow). It only orders turns within the round (see "Initiative").

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Combat: damage, crits, resistances[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Physical attack damage[/b] = random roll between the character's min and max damage (gear included)
  • [b]Monster resistance[/b]: final damage = raw damage × (1 − resistance/100), always at least 1 damage as long as resistance is <100%
  • [b]Damage taken by a hero[/b]: monster hit → possible dodge (no damage) → damage × (1 − reduction/100), where reduction = talent resistance (physical or magic) + Constitution guard, capped at 75 % → the shield absorbs next. A hit that lands always deals at least 1.
  • [b]Initiative[/b]: gauges fill at each participant's speed; the first to reach 100 acts, but nobody acts again until every other living participant has acted (round). On a tie (within 0.5), the side that did not act last goes first.
  • [b]Critical hit[/b]: chance = Dexterity crit (capped at 25%) + the 'Critical' perk of rare items + the mythic set (+10%) + talents + expedition modifier. Damage = [b]×2[/b], plus the items' 'Critical damage' bonus (×2 + value %).
  • [b]Rare-item perks[/b]: [b]spell damage[/b] +x% on single-target spells (not area, not healing) · [b]execute[/b] +x% against a single monster under 25% HP (never area) · [b]bleed[/b] x% chance, on every hit that lands outside area, to poison for 3 turns · [b]thorns[/b] reflects x% of damage taken (minimum 1) · [b]gold[/b] +x% monster gold · [b]last stand[/b] once per combat, a lethal blow leaves 1 HP (after the survival instinct).
  • [b]A hero's school resistances[/b] (physical, fire, ice, nature, holy, shadow): class bonus + resistances of equipped items, limited to −50% … +90%; a negative value is a weakness (more damage). Damage = damage × (1 − resistance/100).
  • [b]Survival instinct[/b]: chance = base (45 / 40 / 35 / 30% by difficulty) + press quality (early +0, good +10, perfect +25, automatic −10) + Constitution above 10 (+1 per point) − 15 if the blow exceeds half the max HP − 10 against an enraged boss, limited to 15% … a cap (90 / 85 / 80 / 75%).
  • [b]Second wind[/b] (exploration): every 6 / 8 / 12 / 20 steps (easy / normal / hard / hardcore), each living hero, neither poisoned nor burning, regains 1% of max HP (+0.1% per Constitution point above 10, ×1.25 for Priest and Druid), up to 60% of max HP; nothing during the 2 steps after a combat, and stepping back onto one of the last 4 cells doesn't count.
  • [b]Base attack stamina cost[/b]: capped at 2 points max regardless of class or admin settings (spells remain freely configurable and can cost more).

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Random dungeon difficulty[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Overall difficulty multiplier[/b] (stats/loot): Easy ×0.6 — Normal ×1 — Hard ×1.7 — Hardcore ×3.0
  • [b]Monster count multiplier[/b] (separate, gentler to stay playable): Easy ×0.7 — Normal ×1 — Hard ×1.35 — Hardcore ×1.8
  • [b]Per-expedition escalation[/b]: every multiplier above is then multiplied by (1 + (run−1)×0.15) — +15% per chained expedition, uncapped
  • [b]Depth bonus[/b] (monster/boss stats): min(i,4)×rate + max(0,i−4)×rate×0.5 — diminishing returns past level 5

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Monsters & bosses (random generation)[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Monsters per level[/b] = round(available rooms ÷ 4 × count multiplier × any expedition modifier)
  • [b]Normal monster base stats[/b]: Strength 8, Dexterity 8, Constitution 6 (+ depth bonus above, ± random variance of 2)
  • [b]Monster groups[/b]: 30% chance a monster spawns as a group (60% of 2 copies, 40% of 3). Each living member is an [b]independent[/b] participant of the round: one action per round, at the monster's speed
  • [b]Monster resistance[/b]: 65% none, 20% physical resistance (10–35%), 15% magic resistance (10–35%)
  • [b]Boss base stats[/b]: Strength 22, Dexterity 16, Constitution 20 (+ depth bonus ×2, ± random variance of 3)
  • [b]Boss position[/b]: always 3 to 6 corridor steps before the exit staircase (never adjacent, never past it), and always deep in the level: its path from the arrival is at least 8 cells and 60% of the path to the exit (never a boss near the start)
  • No normal monster can spawn within 2 tiles of a staircase or archway.

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Loot — drop rates[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Healing potions[/b]: 70% chance per level, 1 to 2 copies (heal = 6 + ⌊i/3⌋×4 + (run−1), tiered every 3 levels so they stack together better)
  • [b]Stamina potions[/b]: 50% chance per level, 1 copy (restore = 12 + ⌊i/3⌋×6 + (run−1)×2, same tiering)
  • [b]Weapon[/b]: 85% chance per level — [b]Armor[/b]: 75% — [b]Jewelry[/b]: 65% (fallback guarantee: if none of the three hit, one is forced at random)
  • [b]Scroll[/b]: 40% chance per level (random spell from the entire game)
  • [b]Fountain[/b]: guaranteed on level 1, then 45% chance per level (forced if 2 straight levels without any fountain)
  • [b]Traps[/b]: 2 to 3 per level; fixed damage (guaranteed minimum) from 2+⌊i×0.8⌋+⌊(run−1)×0.5⌋ to 5+⌊i×1.2⌋+(run−1); actual damage: 15 to 30% of the randomly chosen victim's max HP (+50% on a critical failure)
  • [b]Lockpicking[/b]: chance = 15% + 12% per living Rogue/Thief + 6% per living Assassin + 0.5% per Dexterity point above 10 (max 10 points counted per character); final chance capped between 10 and 95%; d20 threshold = ⌈21 − chance/5⌉; natural 20 = success, natural 1 = critical failure
  • [b]Loot on normal monsters[/b]: round(non-boss monster count × 0.45 × difficulty multiplier) monsters get an item, each with 40–80% drop chance
  • [b]Boss loot[/b]: always guaranteed (weapon/armor/jewelry), with a [b]legendary[/b] chance of 25%×0.6=15% on Normal, 25% on Hard, 45% on Hardcore (× per-expedition escalation, capped at 100%)
  • [b]Secondary stat bonus[/b] (Str/Dex/Con/Int) on an item: 65% chance of 1, 20% chance of 2, 15% none; value = 1–2 + ⌊i/2⌋ + (run−1)
  • [b]Speed bonus[/b]: 12% chance per generated armor/jewelry piece, always [b]flat +1[/b] (never more, never on a weapon, never amplified by difficulty/run/legendary) — deliberately rare and capped since Speed has a linear, immediate effect on combat turn frequency.

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Locked door & secret zone[/color][/font_size]

  • 70% chance a level gets a locked door (if the map is large enough)
  • The door is chosen to [b]guarantee[/b] that at least one room becomes truly unreachable without the key (preference for ≥2 rooms) — never a cosmetic lock that can be walked around
  • The key is [b]never[/b] placed inside the zone it unlocks — always on the accessible side, and never on a staircase (it could not be picked up)
  • Reward inside the locked zone: 40% hidden fountain, otherwise weapon/armor/jewelry with stats boosted [b]+35%[/b] over normal loot, and a legendary chance from 22.5% (Normal) to 55% (Hardcore) × escalation
  • The key to a level's [b]exit archway[/b] (different from the locked door) is always carried by the level's boss, or its toughest monster if there's no boss

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Shop prices[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]Weapon[/b]: 10 + (min damage + max damage)×4
  • [b]Armor / jewelry[/b]: 8 + HP×1.2 + spell damage×5 + (Str+Dex+Con+Int)×3 + (min+max damage)×3
  • [b]Potion[/b]: 3 + heal×0.8 + stamina×0.6
  • [b]Scroll[/b]: fixed price of 30
  • [b]Sell price[/b]: always 50% of the buy price
  • The merchant always offers exactly [b]2[/b] healing potions, [b]2[/b] weapons, [b]2[/b] armor/jewelry pieces and [b]1[/b] scroll per visit — never more (fixed stock, not an unlimited roll)

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Bag[/color][/font_size]

  • [b]12 slots maximum per tab[/b] — Items (weapons/armor/jewelry), Potions, and Keys & scrolls each count independently (36 items possible in total)
  • Strictly identical potions and scrolls stack under a single visual slot (but each still counts as 1 toward its tab's quota)

label: 🛒 The shop
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🛒 The shop[/color][/font_size]

Every defeated monster (and even more so a boss) grants [b]gold[/b], added to a purse shared by the party — shown just above the bag during play.

From the victory screen (once the dungeon is fully completed), the [b]🛒 Visit the shop[/b] button opens a traveling merchant's stall. Each visit offers a different selection of weapons, armor, jewelry, potions and a scroll, whose power scales with your current expedition. Two tabs — [b]For sale[/b] and [b]Your bag[/b] — make it easy to switch between the two.

You can also [b]sell[/b] items from your bag directly from the shop (the "Your bag" tab) — useful to make room or fund a more interesting purchase — for half their value.

Hover (or tap) any item for sale or in your bag to see a [b]detailed tooltip[/b] — full stats for equipment, taught spell and compatible classes for a scroll.

[b]🧙 Traveling merchant[/b]: in a randomly generated dungeon, a merchant also wanders directly through the corridors (usually on level 2), without waiting for the end of the adventure. Spotted by their golden icon once encountered, and then shown on the [b]minimap[/b]. Crossing their tile brings up a prompt to check their stall or continue without stopping — their stock stays the same from one visit to the next (it genuinely depletes if you buy) rather than refreshing every time.

💡 It's a good time to visit the shop right before choosing to continue into a harder dungeon, to best prepare the party.

📊 [b]Effect on the hero.[/b] When you select a weapon, armor or jewel, the right-hand panel compares the item with the chosen hero's current one (« Compare with » buttons), then shows an [b]Effect on <hero>[/b] table: for every statistic that changes (HP, attack, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, speed, crit, dodge, guard, reductions, spell power), the [b]current[/b] value, the value [b]after[/b] equipping and the difference (green ▲, red ▼). The calculation is exactly the game's, caps included. Hover a row: the statistic's detailed card opens, with the calculation and sources (including the item you're eyeing) as if you had equipped it.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Item sheet[/color][/font_size]

An equipment sheet shows [b]all its stats[/b] at the top, as in the inventory: the [b]rarity perk[/b] first, then the bonuses. The [b]Compare with[/b] buttons are laid out in two columns (initial, hero name, class) and the differences table stays below.

label: 🏘️ The village
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🏘️ The village (experimental)[/color][/font_size]

From the victory screen of a randomly generated dungeon, the [b]🏘️ Go to the village[/b] button leads to a small outdoor square — sky, grass, trees — different on every visit (merchant positions and tree density are randomized).

[b]🧙 The merchant[/b] and [b]🔨 the blacksmith[/b] each stand behind their stall, visible from anywhere on the square. The blacksmith offers to [b]upgrade an item you already own[/b] for gold (cost increases with each upgrade, strengthens the bonuses already on the item) — an alternative to having to find a better one.

[b]📖 The Talent Master[/b] lets you reconsider a talent already chosen by any party member: for every tier already unlocked, freely switch to the other option, without waiting for a new level.

Two [b]arches[/b] face each other: one (orange torches) leads to a more powerful dungeon, restarting the usual generation cycle, the other (blue torches) lets you [b]return exactly[/b] to the dungeon you just left. Approaching either always shows a confirmation before leaving.

label: 👹 Monsters and bosses
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]👹 Monsters and bosses[/color][/font_size]

Some monsters have a [b]physical or magic resistance[/b] (reduces damage of the matching type) and may have a [b]special ability[/b] they sometimes use instead of their normal attack.

[b]Bosses[/b] are always noticeably larger on screen, can enter a [b]rage[/b] when their HP drops below a certain threshold (their attacks then become much more violent), and trigger a dedicated combat music track as soon as combat against them actually begins (not just when spotted from a distance).

💪 In random dungeons a boss has [b]far more HP[/b] than a normal monster (×1.8; ×2.2 for the last-level boss), deals 10% more damage and gives 25% more experience and gold (adjustable in Admin, General tab).

Some monsters appear in a [b]group[/b] of 2 or 3 side by side, each with their own HP bar — a group counts as a single turn in the initiative queue, but its higher total HP and improved loot make up for it.

Each monster has its own [b]💨 Speed[/b] stat (see the dedicated topic), which determines how often it gets a turn against your party — independent of how fast it moves through the corridor.

Monsters and bosses move on their own within a [b]patrol zone[/b] around their starting position, and chase you if they spot you — once adjacent, a monster never moves again, it simply waits its turn.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Rage, effects and resistances[/color][/font_size]

🔥 [b]Rage[/b]: any monster may have one (random at generation, or chosen by the level's creator); bosses always have one unless the setting says otherwise. When its HP drop below its threshold, it [b]growls[/b], a red shockwave shakes it and an [b]aura of red flames[/b] wraps around it within moments (same for every monster, boss or not; effects are preloaded when the dungeon loads); its damage increases by the bonus shown on its sheet.

💥 [b]Special ability[/b]: bosses always have one. If the spell has [b]life steal[/b] (drain), the monster heals for that share of the damage dealt.

🩸 [b]Life steal (status)[/b]: the hero hit loses HP each turn for the shown duration, and the monster that inflicted it heals for the drained HP.

🧪 [b]Family effects[/b]: see « Status effects » — poison, burn, sleep… depending on the monster, at random.

🛡️ [b]Resistances per school[/b]: besides physical or magic resistance, a monster may resist (or be weak to) a school of magic, depending on its family: the fire elemental resists fire and fears ice, undead resist shadow and fear holy, golems resist physical damage… A monster of a resistance family (fire elemental, undead, golem…) [b]always[/b] has them, bosses included: only the values differ from one monster to another, and they are never zero (a fire elemental always resists fire, an ice elemental ice). Its sheet lists them (🔥 +50 % · ❄️ −40 %); in combat, « 🛡️ Resists! » or « ⚡ Weakness! » appears when the gap is clear. A negative value is a [b]weakness[/b]: the spell deals more damage.

🕯️ [b]Entering a level[/b]: no monster is placed near the start and all stay calm for about a dozen seconds: you have time to get your bearings.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Numbers, falling and victory[/color][/font_size]

Damage, healing and resistance [b]numbers[/b] stack in readable lines: on the monster for what it takes, just above the hero's card for what the hero takes or receives. A hit monster reacts at the spell's [b]impact[/b] but only falls at the [b]end of the visual effect[/b]. In a group, [b]each monster falls individually[/b] with its own animation and the survivors slide into place. When a boss wipes the party, a dedicated victory sound plays.

label: 📖 Bestiary
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]📖 Bestiary[/color][/font_size]

The third tab of the [b]📊 Statistics[/b] window (icon top-right) is a bestiary that fills in as you win battles. Each monster species you encounter shows its full stats there: Str/Dex/Con, HP, damage, physical/magic resistance, speed, special ability, and how many times you've defeated it.

💡 Bosses are highlighted with a golden border in the list.

label: ⛲ Fountains
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]⛲ Fountains[/color][/font_size]

A fountain restores [b]HP[/b] and [b]stamina[/b] for the whole party, and can even [b]revive[/b] a character who fell in combat. It has a cooldown before it can be used again.

Once discovered, a fountain stays shown on the [b]minimap[/b] (⛲ icon), making it easy to find again.

label: ⚠️ Traps and lockpicking
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]⚠️ Traps and lockpicking[/color][/font_size]

When you arrive on a [b]trap[/b], the game pauses and a window offers to [b]🔓 Pick the lock[/b] or to [b]🚶 Move on[/b] (suffer the trap). You get [b]a single attempt[/b]: no retry after a failure. A fight that was about to start there waits until the window is closed.

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Success chance[/color][/font_size]

The whole party takes part (living characters only). The full calculation is shown before the roll:

  • [b]Base[/b]: 15%
  • [b]Rogue / Thief[/b]: +12% each (stackable)
  • [b]Assassin[/b]: +6% each
  • [b]Dexterity[/b]: +0.5% per point above 10 (up to 10 points counted per character)
  • [b]Caps[/b]: never below 10%, never above 95%

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]The die[/color][/font_size]

A [b]20-sided die[/b] is rolled: you must reach the threshold matching the chance (45% = 12 or more, each winning face being worth 5%). A [b]natural 20[/b] always succeeds, even at 10%; a [b]natural 1[/b] is always a critical failure, even at 95%.

[table=2][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Result[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Effect[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]✨ Perfect lockpicking (20)  [/cell][cell]Trap disarmed, golden glow  [/cell][cell]🔓 Success  [/cell][cell]Trap disarmed: it disappears for good, even a permanent trap  [/cell][cell]❌ Failure  [/cell][cell]The trap goes off as usual  [/cell][cell]💥 Critical failure (1)  [/cell][cell]The trap goes off with [b]+50%[/b] damage  [/cell][/table]

[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]Damage[/color][/font_size]

A living character is [b]picked at random[/b] and loses [b]15 to 30%[/b] of their max HP (the fixed damage set on the trap acts as a minimum). The victim is announced in the window; damage is applied when you click “Continue”.

💡 Chance, bonuses, caps, critical-failure surcharge and damage are set in the administration, “Traps — lockpicking” panel.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Sacrificing an item[/color][/font_size]

When a trap offers to [b]sacrifice an item[/b], you can throw [b]any item from the bag[/b] into the mechanism — potion, scroll, weapon, armor, jewelry — [b]except a key[/b]. The item is consumed and the trap is disarmed for sure.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Trap puzzles[/color][/font_size]

Some traps offer, among their ways out, a [b]puzzle[/b]: no die roll, success depends only on you: a sequence of [b]runes[/b] to repeat, a path to follow over [b]floor tiles[/b], a [b]rope[/b] to cut or a [b]riddle[/b].

  • [b]Ropes[/b]: twisted ropes of different colours link two terminals; the engraved clues point to the right one. One snip of the shears; a cut rope cannot be tied back.
  • [b]Riddles[/b]: a stone tablet poses a riddle with four answers, only one of them right. They are drawn at random from [b]120 riddles[/b] (nature, body, dungeon, creatures, arithmetic…), never repeated within the same window.
  • The number of riddles in a row (1 to 4) and the allowed mistakes are set in the admin, "Traps — methods, puzzles and loot" panel.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Monsters and traps[/color][/font_size]

A monster never crosses a trap that is still active (neither disarmed nor taken), even inside its patrol zone or while chasing you. Disarming a trap reopens the way for monsters.

label: 💾 Saving
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]💾 Saving your game[/color][/font_size]

The game offers [b]10 independent save slots[/b], accessible via the « Save slots » banner on the home screen and via the in-game Save menu. Each keeps its own dungeon and its own party: enough to run several games in parallel without them stepping on each other.

On every save, the [b]slot picker[/b] opens: you choose where to save. Each slot shows a summary (dungeon title, [b]dungeon type[/b] — Original, Random or Custom —, characters' level, save date) and offers [b]Load[/b], [b]Overwrite[/b] (for an already-used slot) or [b]Delete[/b]. An hourglass is shown while saving.

⚠️ Save slots are [b]purged with every new version (build) of the game[/b]: this guarantees a loaded game always benefits from the latest fixes. A class change made in the admin, however, is applied automatically when a save is resumed.

The Save menu also offers: [b]Export[/b], which downloads a complete JSON file (game + dungeon configuration) to keep or [b]import[/b] later, even on another device; and "Link a file" (if your browser allows it), which automatically syncs the current game to a local file on every save.

On the home screen, two discreet links also let you resume a game another way: « Import a JSON file » (an exported game) and « Load a dungeon from a code »: paste a long text code you received (generated by whoever created the dungeon, or by yourself via admin) and a new game starts directly with that configuration. It's handy for sharing a dungeon in a conversation, with no file to attach. A dungeon loaded this way can be played but not edited (admin stays locked) — to edit a received dungeon, ask for the JSON file instead.

label: 🔊 Sound settings
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🔊 Sound settings[/color][/font_size]

Top-right of the game screen: the [b]🔊[/b] icon opens the sound panel, which combines a checkbox to [b]mute all sound[/b] with separate sliders for [b]sound effects[/b] and [b]ambient music[/b] volume (which changes with the level's visual theme).

Every spell has its [b]own sound[/b] (one file per spell); the basic attack, a [b]boss victory[/b] (two sounds, alternating by boss), life and stamina [b]potions[/b] and the [b]fountain[/b] have theirs too. All sounds are loaded once when the game starts, not when entering a dungeon.

label: ⚙ Settings
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]⚙ Settings[/color][/font_size]

The [b]⚙ Settings[/b] button in the top bar opens a window with six tabs. Every setting is remembered.

[b]Graphics[/b] — [b]graphics quality[/b] is chosen among [b]Auto, Low, Medium, High, Ultra[/b] or [b]Custom[/b]. In [b]Auto[/b] mode the game measures your machine at each launch and sets the quality to aim for at least 60 frames per second. [b]Automatic adaptation[/b] lowers quality one notch when the game drops below the target frame rate and raises it again when the machine keeps up (unavailable in Custom). The [b]detailed options[/b] are set by hand: 3D resolution, anti-aliasing (MSAA), anisotropic filtering, torches with light, particle amount, dynamic spell glows, view distance, textures (Standard 1024 or High 2048 — only the PC version ships the 2048 textures) and banner flames.

[b]Display[/b] — [b]Fullscreen / Windowed[/b] ([b]F11[/b] or [b]Alt+Enter[/b] also toggle), [b]vertical sync[/b] (V-Sync) and [b]frame rate limit[/b] (lower = less heat and battery use). The [b]update[/b] settings are here too (see “Versions and updates”). In the browser, the window and sync are handled by the browser itself.

[b]Sound[/b] — sound effect and ambient music volumes, and a global mute (see also “Sound settings”).

[b]Controls[/b] — every key of the game can be rebound; defaults are WASD in English and ZQSD in French.

[b]Accessibility[/b] — [b]Reduced motion[/b], which softens flame and light flicker.

[b]Diagnostics[/b] — your machine (graphics card, renderer, platform, memory, processors), the [b]recommended level[/b], live measurements (frames per second, current level, 3D resolution, last adjustment), the launch calibration result, the [b]Re-run detection[/b] button, the [b]Reset graphics settings[/b] button and the FPS / RAM / VRAM counter (checkbox in the Diagnostics tab, or the F3 key).

💡 Game running badly? Switch to [b]Low[/b] or let [b]Auto[/b] work: it lowers the 3D resolution on its own before degrading anything else.

[font_size=17][color=#e8b45c]Survival instinct[/color][/font_size]

In ⚙ Settings: the [b]mode[/b] (On: you press; Auto: the game reacts for you with a reduced chance; Off) and the [b]window length[/b] (×1, ×1.5 or ×2). No effect in ranked runs. See the ⚔️ Combat topic.

label: 👤 Online account
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]👤 Online account[/color][/font_size]

The [b]online account[/b] is [b]optional and free[/b]. The [b]👤 Account[/b] button (top bar) shows your nickname once signed in.

[b]Create an account[/b] — enter an [b]e-mail[/b], a [b]nickname[/b] and a [b]password[/b].
  • Nickname: 3 to 20 characters — letters, digits, [b]_[/b] and [b]-[/b]; it must be free. It is the only name other players see.
  • Password: 8 characters minimum.
  • Your e-mail is [b]never displayed[/b] or given to other players.
  • A [b]confirmation e-mail[/b] is sent: click the link it contains, then sign in. Check your spam folder if needed.

[b]Sign in[/b] — e-mail + password. The session is remembered: you stay signed in from one launch to the next. If the connection cannot be checked (offline), your session is simply kept.

[b]Forgot password[/b] — enter your e-mail first, then press “Forgot password”: a reset e-mail is sent if the account exists.

[b]Sign out[/b] — clears the session on this device; your online data stays.

[b]Delete my account[/b] — [b]permanent[/b]: your account and online data (sent runs, rankings, rewards, chat messages…) are erased. Your saves on the device are untouched.

[b]What the account unlocks[/b]: challenges and rankings, ranked runs, experience, badges and cosmetics (see “Challenges and ranked runs” and “Experience, badges and cosmetics”), the players' chat.

💡 If an error mentions too many requests (sign-ups or e-mails), wait a few minutes and try again: e-mail sending is limited to prevent abuse.

label: 🏆 Challenges and ranked runs
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🏆 Challenges and ranked runs[/color][/font_size]

The big [b]Random Dungeon[/b] seal on the home screen opens the [b]Online mode[/b] window (when the online service is available). All connected play is arranged in [b]four tabs[/b]: [b]🎮 Play[/b] (four cards: Free run, Ranked run, Weekly Challenge, Monthly Hardcore, each with its rules and launch button), [b]🏆 Rankings[/b], [b]🏅 Rewards[/b] and [b]📜 My runs[/b]. A banner at the top shows your nickname, level and XP, with shortcuts [b]💬 Chat[/b], [b]👤 Account[/b] and [b]❓ How does it work?[/b]. Without an account the game stays playable: the “Sign in” button leads to the account.

[b]Four kinds of rankings[/b]
  • [b]Open challenges[/b] — each challenge has its own criterion (levels cleared, points…). When signed in, your best random-dungeon run is [b]sent automatically[/b] (“🏆 Score sent to the ranking”). These scores are [b]declared by the game and not verified[/b]; a [b]✔[/b] marks a verified score. To be ranked, clear at least one level.
  • [b]Ranked runs[/b] — one ranking per difficulty, [b]100% verified[/b].
  • [b]Weekly Challenge[/b] — one dungeon and one special rule per week, unlimited attempts, [b]100% verified[/b].
  • [b]Monthly Hardcore[/b] — a single dungeon, the same for everyone, for a month, [b]100% verified[/b].

[b]How a score is verified[/b]: for a ranked run, the [b]server picks the dungeon[/b] (you don't) and your game records a [b]log of all your actions[/b]. At the end the log is sent; the server [b]replays the run identically[/b] with the same rules and [b]recomputes the score[/b]. What the game claims therefore does not matter: only the replay counts. Verification takes [b]a few minutes[/b] — until then the run is “pending”. Offline, the log is kept and sent again at the next opportunity.

[b]Ranked runs[/b] (in the [b]🎮 Play[/b] tab, “Ranked run” card: pick the difficulty, then launch)
[table=3][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Difficulty[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Dungeon[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]XP multiplier[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]Easy  [/cell][cell]3 levels, 13 × 11  [/cell][cell]×1  [/cell][cell]Normal  [/cell][cell]3 levels, 13 × 11  [/cell][cell]×1.5  [/cell][cell]Hard  [/cell][cell]3 levels, 13 × 11  [/cell][cell]×2  [/cell][cell]Hardcore  [/cell][cell]3 levels, 13 × 11  [/cell][cell]×3  [/cell][/table]
  • [b]Score[/b] = levels cleared; on a tie, the [b]faster[/b] run ranks higher. The ranking keeps your [b]best verified run[/b] of each difficulty.
  • Attempts are [b]unlimited[/b] (up to 40 runs started per 24 h); starting a new ranked run abandons the previous unfinished one.
  • [b]Ranked-run rules[/b]: no administration, no export, no reloading an old save (a save works only once). Any off-rules action makes the run [b]unrankable[/b]: it plays normally but is not sent.
  • Reward: [b]40 × levels cleared × multiplier[/b] experience points per verified run.

[b]Weekly Challenge[/b] (“📅 Weekly Challenge” card)
  • Every [b]Monday[/b] (Paris time) a [b]special rule[/b] changes how you play: 🏕️ No Rest, 🥂 Glass Cannon, 🧍 Lone Hero, 🗡️ Steel Only, 👹 Monster Den, 🌪️ Frenzy, 🌫️ Thick Fog, 💀 Limited Stamina. The eight rules rotate in that order; the card shows the current rule, the time left and next week's rule.
  • The dungeon (4 levels, 13 × 11, Normal difficulty) is [b]the same for everyone[/b], drawn at the week's first run.
  • Attempts are [b]unlimited[/b]: only your [b]best verified result[/b] counts (levels cleared, then time). Starting again abandons the previous unfinished run.
  • The ranking is 100% replay-verified and closes at the end of the week with its [b]rank badges[/b] (see “Experience, badges and cosmetics”). You leave the run as in a ranked run (pause or finish here).

[b]Monthly Hardcore[/b]
  • A [b]single dungeon per month[/b] (5 levels, 15 × 13, maximum difficulty), identical for all players, drawn at the month's first run.
  • [b]One attempt per day[/b] (Paris day). The attempt is [b]used up at launch[/b], even if you give up: a confirmation reminds you.
  • The month's ranking only counts [b]replay-verified[/b] runs; it ends with the month and then awards [b]rank badges[/b] (see “Experience, badges and cosmetics”).
  • Hover the badges in the Rewards tab to see the titles, frames, nickname colours and experience to win.

[b]Leaving a ranked run[/b] — you can stop [b]at any time[/b] with “Back to menu”; a window then explains each choice:
  • [b]⏸ Pause[/b]: the run is saved and stays in progress; it can be resumed [b]only once[/b] from the save.
  • [b]📤 Finish here[/b]: the run is sent as it stands and verified; [b]only the levels already cleared count[/b] and the run can no longer be resumed. With no level cleared the button becomes “Give up”: nothing is ranked.
  • In the monthly Hardcore, the day's attempt is [b]already used[/b] whatever you choose.
In a free run while signed in, your progress is sent automatically when you leave.

💡 Best strategy: practise in a random dungeon or an Easy ranked run, then try the monthly Hardcore with a well-prepared party — you only get one attempt per day.

label: 🏅 Experience, badges and cosmetics
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🏅 Experience, badges and cosmetics[/color][/font_size]

Each [b]verified[/b] ranked run earns [b]account experience[/b] (XP). The [b]🏅 Rewards[/b] tab of the “Online mode” window shows your level, your XP, how much is missing for the next level, your badge collection and your equipped cosmetics.

[b]Account level[/b] — it follows total XP: level 2 at 100 XP, level 3 at 400 XP, level 4 at 900 XP, level 5 at 1,600 XP… (level = 1 + square root of XP ÷ 100). Your level shows next to your nickname in the rankings and in the chat. It has [b]no effect on gameplay[/b].

[b]XP sources[/b]
[table=2][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]Source[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell][b][color=#d9b56e]XP[/color][/b]  [/cell][cell]Verified ranked run  [/cell][cell]40 × levels cleared × difficulty multiplier (×1 / ×1.5 / ×2 / ×3)  [/cell][cell]Monthly Hardcore — each verified attempt  [/cell][cell]+50 XP  [/cell][cell]Monthly Hardcore — 3 levels cleared  [/cell][cell]+150 XP (once)  [/cell][cell]Monthly Hardcore — 5 levels cleared  [/cell][cell]+400 XP (once)  [/cell][cell]Weekly Challenge — at least one level cleared  [/cell][cell]+100 XP (per week)  [/cell][cell]Weekly Challenge — all 4 levels cleared  [/cell][cell]+250 XP (once per rule)  [/cell][cell]Weekly Challenge — final rank  [/cell][cell]600 / 400 / 250 XP (podium), 120 (top 10), 30 (others)  [/cell][/table]

[b]Badges[/b] — distinctions to collect, ever rarer:
  • 🔥 [b]Into the Furnace[/b] — played the monthly Hardcore (title “Daredevil”).
  • ⛏️ [b]Three Floors Down[/b] — cleared 3 levels in the monthly Hardcore (title “Delver”).
  • 🕳️ [b]Heart of the Abyss[/b] — cleared 5 levels (title “Abyssal”).
  • 🎖️ [b]Among the Best[/b] — finished a month in the top 10%.
  • 🏅 [b]Top Ten[/b], 🥉 [b]Third of the Month[/b], 🥈 [b]Runner-up of the Month[/b], 👑 [b]Champion of the Month[/b] — awarded when the month closes, according to your rank.
  • 📅 [b]Weekly Challenge badges[/b] — one badge (and title) per rule cleared across all 4 levels: 🏕️ Ascetic, 🥂 Tightrope Walker, 🧍 Lone Wolf, 🗡️ Bare Blade, 👹 Exterminator, 🌪️ Storm Heart, 🌫️ Phantom, 💀 Long-Distance Runner; then when the week closes: 🏅 Brave of the Week (top 10), 🥉 🥈 and 👑 Master of the Week (podium).
Rank badges are earned [b]once per month or per week[/b]; depth milestones and rule badges are permanent.

[b]Streaks and legends[/b]
  • 🔗 [b]Dedicated[/b] (3 weeks in a row), 🌠 [b]True to the Post[/b] (6) and 🌌 [b]Unshakable[/b] (12, +500 XP, “aurora” frame) reward regular play of the Weekly Challenge. The challenge card shows your streak and the next milestone; skipping a week resets it.
  • 🏛 [b]Hall of Legends[/b] (Rankings › Legends): the champion of every weekly challenge and every Hardcore month stays there for good.
  • 🔓 [b]Unlocked rules[/b]: clearing a challenge rule in full (Glass Cannon, Frenzy, Lone Hero, Steel Only) makes it available as an expedition modifier in free runs, marked 🔓.
  • [b]Hero ring[/b]: each rule, streak or champion badge grants a ring colour for the party portraits (Rewards tab). Kept on this device, purely decorative.

[b]Cosmetics[/b] — each badge may grant a [b]title[/b], a [b]frame[/b] or a [b]nickname colour[/b]. In the [b]Rewards[/b] tab, pick what you equip (or “— None —”) and confirm with [b]Equip[/b]. They show in the rankings, and the colour and level in the chat. They are [b]purely decorative[/b]: no effect on runs.

💡 The administrator's test runs give no XP or badge and appear in no ranking.

label: 💬 The chat
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]💬 The chat[/color][/font_size]

The [b]💬 Chat[/b] button (top bar) opens the players' chat. You must be [b]signed in[/b] to read as well as to write; otherwise the window offers to open your account.

[b]The charter[/b] — the first time, you must read and [b]accept the chat charter[/b] (respect, nothing illegal or advertising, no personal data, 30-day retention, moderation). Without acceptance there is no reading or writing: the server checks it too. If the charter changes, it is shown again once. “Decline and close” simply closes the window.

[b]Rooms[/b] — three tabs: [b]General[/b], [b]Français[/b] and [b]English[/b]. The room of your game language opens by default. Messages update [b]by themselves[/b]; the list scrolls to the newest message unless you scrolled back, and keeps the latest 150 on screen.

[b]Writing[/b] — type in the input box then [b]Enter[/b] or [b]Send[/b]. Each message shows the time, the nickname (with its cosmetic colour and account level), then the text, [b]always as plain text[/b]. Rules enforced by the server:
  • [b]300 characters[/b] maximum; extra spaces and invisible characters removed.
  • [b]One message every 3 seconds[/b] and 15 per minute at most.
  • No two [b]identical[/b] messages within 30 seconds.
  • A [b]forbidden-word filter[/b] refuses abusive messages.
  • If the administrator has [b]muted[/b] you, you cannot write until the time shown.
Error messages tell you exactly what was refused; your text stays in the input box.

[b]Private messages[/b] — [b]✉ Private[/b] tab: your conversations (last message, unread count). To write to a player, open the [b]⋯[/b] menu on one of their messages in a room, then [b]✉ Private message[/b]. Same rules as the rooms (300 characters, rate, filter, mute) and at most [b]20 new contacts per day[/b]. The [b]Accept private messages[/b] switch closes them: nobody can write to you. A player you block can no longer write to you; a received private message can be reported.

[b]Red bubble[/b] — a red dot appears on the [b]💬 Chat[/b] button (top bar, “Online mode” window) and on the tabs when there is news: unread private messages, or new room messages since your last visit. It clears when you read. The game asks the server every 30 seconds.

[b]Report and block[/b] — each other player's message has a [b]⋯[/b] menu:
  • [b]Report message[/b] — sent to the administrator (20 reports per day at most).
  • [b]Block this player[/b] — their messages disappear for you. The [b]Blocked players[/b] button lists your blocks and lets you [b]Unblock[/b].

[b]Moderation[/b] — the administrator can delete a message, mute a player for a set time, or dismiss a report, and maintains the forbidden-word list.

[b]Privacy[/b] — room messages are visible to all signed-in players; a private message can only be read by you and your correspondent (and by the administrator if reported). All are kept [b]30 days[/b] then deleted, and erased with your account if you delete it.

label: 🛠 The editor and testing
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🛠 The editor (Admin) and testing[/color][/font_size]

The [b]🛠 Admin[/b] button in the top bar opens the [b]dungeon editor[/b]: you modify a dungeon's characters, classes, spells, items and levels, then test it. The creation tutorial (the “New here?” link on the home screen, or its “Test” section) covers each screen.

[b]Where is it available?[/b]
  • In “[b]Create your own dungeon[/b]”: open from the start, it is its purpose.
  • In a [b]random dungeon[/b] and in the [b]Original Dungeon[/b]: the button is visible in game; the editor then asks for the dungeon's [b]administrator password[/b].
  • In a dungeon loaded from a code: it stays inaccessible (ask for the JSON file to edit instead).

[b]Testing freely[/b] — outside a ranked run, the editor has [b]no limit and no consequence[/b]: you can modify a dungeon, restart it, change the party, give yourself items, test a trap or a boss as often as you like. It affects neither the rankings nor your experience.

[b]Ranked runs[/b] — the one exception: using the editor during a ranked run makes it [b]unrankable[/b] (it plays, but is not sent), because the server must be able to replay it identically.

[b]Sharing a dungeon[/b] — “📋 Generate a code to share” produces a long text to paste into a conversation: whoever loads it (“Load a dungeon from a code”, on the home screen) plays your dungeon without any file to attach. To let them edit it too, send the JSON export instead.

label: 🔄 Versions and updates
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🔄 Versions and updates[/color][/font_size]

[b]Version number[/b] — at the bottom of the home screen; a click opens the [b]version log[/b], listing all the changes. After an update, a [b]✨ What's new[/b] window summarises them once.

[b]Automatic updates[/b] (PC versions) — at launch, the game looks for a newer version. If there is one, a window offers [b]Update[/b], [b]Later[/b] or [b]Ignore this version[/b]; only the modified files are downloaded, the game restarts, and your saves are kept. If it fails, the release page opens for a manual download.

In [b]⚙ Settings › Display › Updates[/b]: [b]Check for updates at launch[/b] (on by default), [b]Include pre-releases[/b] (for testers) and [b]Check now[/b].

[b]Web version[/b] — it updates itself with the website: nothing to do.

💡 Ranked runs are always replayed with the rules of [b]their own game version[/b]: an update never skews the rankings.

label: 🛡️ Online administration
text:
[font_size=20][color=#e8b45c]🛡️ Online administration[/color][/font_size]

An [b]administrator[/b] account looks after the online side. Here, in full transparency, is what it can do — and cannot do.

[b]It can[/b]
  • Launch [b]test runs[/b] to check the game: they don't use up its daily attempt, appear in no ranking and give no XP or badge.
  • View [b]overall statistics[/b]: number of accounts and active players, runs per mode, verification queue, rejection reasons, chat activity.
  • [b]Moderate the chat[/b]: handle reported messages (delete, mute for 24 h, dismiss), unmute, and maintain the forbidden-word list.

[b]It cannot[/b]
  • See your [b]e-mail[/b] or your password.
  • Change a score, a verified run or your rewards.
  • Pretend to be you: the role is stored on the server, and every administration action is re-checked there.

💡 Abusive behaviour in the chat? Use [b]⋯ › Report message[/b]: it is this report that lets the administrator act.
